page: Microsoft Azure E32ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDSv5 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C x86_64 processor operating at 2.8 GHz, featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. For local storage, it includes a 1229 GB local disk and supports Premium Storage. It runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations show average performance across most compute and memory metrics. The instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1900.09 and a multi-core score of 31080.73. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 1678.79 GB/sec for small cached blocks, dropping to 143.87 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 67.31 GB/sec for large uncached writes. In database operations, the server processed 15337.83 operations per second on PassMark and handled 31.13 million operations per second in Redis SET tests.

While the server demonstrates strong performance in small-model LLM text generation at 278.54 tokens per second, it exhibits a clear tradeoff in larger AI workloads, dropping to a weak 6.67 tokens per second for 70B model prompt processing, with no data available for 70B text generation. This indicates it is not optimized for large-scale AI inference. However, its high memory density and local storage make it highly cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads without requiring expensive GPU resources. It is best suited for database hosting, software compilation, static web serving, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
